pronoun_cases.prompt: Which form is the best starting point in this scene?

options: तू कहाँ है? · tū kahā̃ hai?

आप कहाँ हैं? · āp kahā̃ haĩ?

pronoun_cases.prompt: What would help you make a better choice?

Assuming everyone prefers the form your friends use.
pronoun_cases.why: Context and expressed preference help you choose. Your own familiar pattern is useful experience, but it is not a universal rule.

review_fixtures.title: A confident answer to an incomplete question
review_fixtures.draft: Translate “you” into Hindi. Correct answer: तुम. Reject all other answers.
review_fixtures.issue: Missing relationship and setting; falsely narrow answer key.
review_fixtures.revision: At a first meeting, you want a respectful way to address an unfamiliar adult. Choose the best starting form: आप / तुम / तू.
review_fixtures.reason: Make the target interpretable before scoring it.

review_fixtures.title: The universal family
review_fixtures.draft: Always use तू with family members.
review_fixtures.issue: An absolute cultural rule erases variation between families and relationships.
review_fixtures.revision: In this dialogue, two siblings have told us they use तू with each other. Interpret its use in that scene; do not generalize to all families.
review_fixtures.reason: Give a particular relationship; remove the universal claim.

review_fixtures.title: The polite pronoun, the wrong agreement
review_fixtures.draft: Target: standard agreement. Model answer: आप कहाँ हो?
review_fixtures.issue: The model answer conflicts with the standard pattern this item is teaching.
review_fixtures.revision: For this standard-pattern exercise, use आप कहाँ हैं? Add a reviewer note that real-world variation requires contextual judgment.
review_fixtures.reason: Keep the target pattern consistent without declaring all other usage illegitimate.

review_fixtures.title: A vowel sign takes a wrong turn
review_fixtures.draft: कि is pronounced ik because the vowel mark appears first.
review_fixtures.issue: It mistakes visual position for spoken order.
review_fixtures.revision: कि is ki. The short-i sign appears on the left of the consonant, but the vowel is read after it.
review_fixtures.reason: Correct the underlying misconception, not just the selected option.

review_fixtures.title: A reading lesson becomes a vocabulary test
review_fixtures.draft: Objective: distinguish ि and ी. Task: translate an unfamiliar paragraph and infer the speaker’s mood.
review_fixtures.issue: The task adds vocabulary and inference demands unrelated to the narrow objective.
review_fixtures.revision: First distinguish कि and की. Then apply the same contrast to मि and मी. Assess paragraph comprehension separately.
review_fixtures.reason: Change one demand at a time before increasing task complexity.

review_fixtures.title: An item with a defensible target
review_fixtures.draft: Objective: standard agreement with तुम. Prompt: Complete तुम कहाँ ___? Options: है / हो / हैं. Key: हो. Feedback: In this pattern, तुम pairs with हो.
review_fixtures.issue: No intentionally planted defect in this fixture; scope and answer key are explicit.
review_fixtures.revision: Retain the item for independent educator review. Approval in this demonstration is not production sign-off.
review_fixtures.reason: A review system must allow sound items through, not only find faults.
